title: Lexitas Pricing
summary: A breakdown of Lexitas pricing in 2026, including Record Insights at $0.25 per page, reported retrieval turnaround, and how flat fee platforms like Codes Health bundle retrieval, AI chronologies, and completeness verification.
body_markdown:
Medical record retrieval can eat a real share of a law firm's pre litigation budget, yet plenty of firms have little visibility into what they are actually paying for and what they are getting back. For plaintiff attorneys handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, and wrongful death matters, understanding how a vendor like Lexitas structures pricing is central to controlling cost without blowing up case timelines.[AI-powered medical record retrieval](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) platforms have introduced models that bundle services traditionally sold separately, which makes apples to apples comparison harder but also opens room to cut total cost of ownership.


This guide breaks down Lexitas pricing, explains what drives retrieval costs, and helps litigation teams figure out whether a traditional vendor or a specialized AI powered platform fits their workflow and budget.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Lexitas does not appear to publish a standard base rate for its main record retrieval service on its current public pages, so firms need to request a quote to compare


-


Lexitas Record Insights, its AI chronology service, is currently priced at $0.25 per uploaded page as an introductory rate, with standard delivery in 2 to 5 business days


-


Lexitas reports a 30 to 45 day average turnaround for record retrieval, and Record Insights summaries are delivered after records are submitted for analysis


-


AI analysis sold as a per page add on creates cost that scales with volume; a 5,000 page case adds $1,250 for chronology generation alone


-


Flat fee pricing that folds in AI chronologies and completeness verification removes invoice variability and makes budgeting predictable


-


Incomplete authorizations are the number one cause of denied requests, and pre submission AI validation prevents the restart cycle that rejected authorizations trigger


-


Vendors advertising same day retrieval typically return only what is already available electronically, leaving your staff and client to chase the rest, which drives client frustration and churn


## **Understanding Medical Record Retrieval Costs for Law Firms**


Medical record retrieval is one of the most time intensive and cost variable parts of plaintiff litigation. For practices handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability, insurance litigation, and wrongful death cases, records are the evidentiary foundation for case valuation, demand preparation, expert review, and trial strategy.


### **Why Pricing Transparency Matters for Litigation Teams**


Plenty of firms learn their true retrieval cost only when the invoice lands. Traditional pricing tends to involve several moving parts:


-


Per page charges that scale unpredictably with record volume


-


Facility fees passed through from healthcare providers


-


Rush charges for expedited requests


-


Add on services like chronologies, summaries, or analysis sold separately


-


Re retrieval costs when the first request comes back incomplete


For high volume practices, those variables create real month to month budget swing. A firm handling 100 cases a year averaging 1,000 pages each faces very different economics depending on whether AI analysis sits inside base pricing or gets billed at $0.25 per page as its own line item.


### **Lexitas's Position in the Market**


Lexitas has operated since 1987 and built a full service litigation support ecosystem covering court reporting, process serving, legal staffing, and[medical record retrieval](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/lexitas-reviews) . That breadth appeals to firms that want one vendor relationship across several litigation support needs, and it retrieves medical, billing, radiology, pathology, pharmacy, and other record types.


The flip side of a diversified model is that record retrieval sits alongside several other service lines. Firms whose main bottleneck is record speed and completeness, rather than deposition scheduling or process serving, may weigh[specialized retrieval platforms](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/lexitas-reviews) differently.


## **How Case Management Integration Influences Retrieval Pricing**


Integration has become a real factor in vendor value. When retrieval lives outside the case file, legal teams deal with:


-


**Context switching** between case management and vendor portals


-


**Manual status tracking** through email, phone calls, and separate dashboards


-


**Document re upload** to get records into the case file


-


**Communication fragmentation** across systems


Both vendors address this. Lexitas has an official Filevine integration, and according to Lexitas, users can order records, view request status in real time, access client records, and see associated record fees inside Filevine, which the company says removes the need to switch platforms.


### **The Value of Embedded Retrieval Workflows**


Codes Health's Filevine partnership embeds retrieval directly into Filevine case projects as well. Legal teams can:


-


Submit retrieval requests from within the relevant case file


-


Track request status and provider outreach in real time


-


Communicate with the retrieval team without leaving the case workflow


-


Receive completed records, billing materials, and analysis in the project


-


Review retrieval history and completeness status in one place


Since both platforms offer a Filevine path, the useful comparison is what each integration actually does day to day and how much administrative overhead it removes. Beyond Filevine,[Codes Health also offers](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/lexitas-reviews) custom integrations with other case management systems, CRM platforms, and medical software for high volume customers, which matters for firms that do not want another portal and another set of credentials.


## **Pricing Models for AI Powered Chronologies and Insights**


One of the bigger pricing distinctions in this market is how vendors charge for AI analysis: the work that organizes records chronologically, extracts key medical facts, and surfaces litigation relevant patterns.


### **Lexitas Record Insights Pricing Structure**


Lexitas sells its AI chronology service, Record Insights, as a separate add on:


-


**$0.25 per uploaded page** , listed as an introductory rate


-


**2 to 5 business days** delivery for standard requests


-


**Up to 7 business days** for uploads exceeding 15,000 pages


-


**Excel export** with AI enabled chronological organization, plus search and AI Insights


Per page pricing is predictable within a case but scales quickly across complex matters:


-


**100 pages:** $25, delivered in 2 to 5 business days


-


**500 pages:** $125, delivered in 2 to 5 business days


-


**1,000 pages:** $250, delivered in 2 to 5 business days


-


**5,000 pages:** $1,250, delivered in 2 to 5 business days


-


**15,000 pages and up:** $3,750 and up, delivered in up to 7 business days


A firm handling 100 cases a year averaging 1,000 pages each would run roughly $25,000 in Record Insights fees at the current introductory rate, assuming all 100,000 pages get submitted, and that sits on top of base retrieval fees.


### **Flat Fee Models with Included Analysis**


The alternative approach folds analysis into the retrieval service. Codes Health uses a flat fee model that includes AI automated case chronologies and document summarization with no per page charge for analysis, combining retrieval and AI review within the same platform and pricing model. That structure offers:


-


Budget predictability without invoice variability tied to page count


-


Breach of care flagging that surfaces standard of care deviations for attorney and expert review


-


Missing Record Review that verifies completeness before delivery


-


Human verified analysis, with medical and legal specialists reviewing outputs


For practices where analysis is standard on every case, bundling removes the per matter decision about whether to order a chronology at all.


General purpose tools like ChatGPT can pull basic information out of a document, but[these platforms are](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) not built for litigation grade medical record review and cannot analyze medical records with the precision this work requires. They do not provide the integrated retrieval, authorization validation, completeness review, provider follow up, and human verification workflow that a purpose built platform like Codes Health delivers.


## **Comparing Retrieval Costs: Speed vs. Traditional Methods**


Turnaround affects litigation economics directly. Every week waiting on records pushes back demand letters, expert engagement, negotiation, and resolution. The cost of delay is harder to quantify than a retrieval invoice, but it often exceeds it.


### **Reported Retrieval Timelines**


Lexitas currently reports a 30 to 45 day average turnaround for record retrieval. Record Insights summaries are delivered within 2 to 5 business days after records are submitted for analysis, or up to 7 business days for uploads above 15,000 pages. Lexitas does not publish a combined end to end figure, so firms planning around a single number should confirm expected timing for their own matters.


### **AI Powered Retrieval Speed**


Specialized platforms have compressed these timelines.[Codes Health delivers](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-lexitas-alternatives) complete records with AI analysis in a couple of weeks, including chronologies, summaries, and completeness verification, all under one flat fee.


Worth saying plainly: fast is not the same as complete. Services promising same day retrieval typically return only the records already sitting in electronic portals, which leaves your staff or your client tracking down everything else. That extra client involvement is a reliable source of frustration and a known driver of churn. Codes Health does not offer same day delivery. It works toward the complete record set in a couple of weeks rather than the months manual workflows can take.


### **Calculating the Cost of Delay**


For a personal injury matter moving toward settlement, a slower retrieval cycle carries costs that never show up on a retrieval invoice:


-


Additional case carrying costs in staff time and overhead allocation


-


Delayed attorney fee realization affecting firm cash flow


-


Extended statute of limitations exposure on time sensitive matters


-


Client satisfaction issues from prolonged uncertainty


## **Pricing for Medical, Billing, and Imaging Requests**


Complete case documentation takes more than clinical notes. Damages analysis, case valuation, demand preparation, and trial strategy all depend on medical records documenting diagnosis and treatment, billing records establishing economic damages, and imaging supporting injury documentation.


### **Single Source vs. Multi Vendor Approaches**


Some services handle clinical records but route billing documentation or imaging through separate requests or separate vendors. That fragmentation creates:


-


Multiple authorization forms across different vendors


-


Inconsistent status tracking and separate follow up processes


-


Timing misalignment when records arrive at different intervals


-


Higher total cost from overlapping administrative overhead


Codes Health supports[medical, billing, and imaging](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/lexitas-reviews) requests through a unified workflow, so litigation teams can consolidate retrieval activity for the full case file.


### **Provider Fee Pass Through Considerations**


Whatever vendor you use, healthcare providers charge facility fees for record production, and those vary by state, provider type, and format. When comparing pricing, confirm whether provider fees are included in quoted rates or added separately, how the vendor handles fee disputes, whether you get visibility into provider fee schedules, and how re retrieval affects cumulative charges.


## **Determining Value: The AI and Human Hybrid Approach**


The accuracy of AI generated analysis determines its litigation value. A chronology with errors, omissions, or mischaracterized medical facts costs attorney or paralegal time to verify and fix, which eats the efficiency that justified buying it.


### **What Each Platform Documents**


Lexitas's public Record Insights materials describe NLP and AI enabled analysis, chronologies, summaries, AI Insights, search, and Excel output. Those materials, as reviewed, do not specify whether AI generated outputs receive human verification before delivery, so that is a question worth asking directly.


Codes Health pairs AI processing with human verification, where medical, legal, and operational specialists review outputs before they reach the firm. That hybrid model:


-


Addresses hallucination concerns that affect pure AI systems


-


Catches extraction errors before they reach case materials


-


Validates medical terminology against the actual record content


-


Confirms that returned materials match the original request


The pricing question for litigation teams becomes simple: what does verifying AI output internally cost you, compared with paying for analysis that arrives already verified?


### **Authorization Quality and Rejection Prevention**


Incomplete authorizations are the number one cause of denied retrieval requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records will restart the clock on your request. Codes Health's AI review checks[authorizations before submission](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/lexitas-reviews) and automatically flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


The usual culprits:


-


Missing patient signatures


-


Unclear or expired authorization dates


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive record categories (mental health, HIV, substance abuse)


-


Misspelled patient or provider names


-


Missing dates of service


Pre submission validation is value that never shows up in a per request rate but hits your total time to records directly.


## **Factors Influencing Retrieval Costs: What to Ask For**


When evaluating vendors, whether Lexitas, Codes Health, or anyone else, get clarity on the dimensions that actually move total cost of ownership.


-


**Base retrieval structure:** Is pricing per request, per facility, per page, or flat fee per case? Are there minimums or setup fees? How are provider pass through fees handled? What happens when the first retrieval comes back incomplete?


-


**AI analysis pricing:** Is chronology generation included or an add on? If separate, what is the per page or per request charge? How much time does analysis add? Is AI output verified by humans before delivery?


-


**Completeness and quality:** Does the service verify records against the original request before delivery? How are missing facilities or date ranges identified? What is the process for supplemental records? Is Missing Record Review part of the service?


-


**Integration and workflow:** Which case management platforms does the service connect to? Is the integration embedded or does it require portal switching? Can communications and status stay in the case file? How are completed records delivered?


-


**Volume and contract terms:** Are volume arrangements available? What contract length is required? How does pricing handle variable monthly volume?


### **Red Flags in Retrieval Pricing**


A few structures deserve extra scrutiny: no ballpark pricing available at all, per page charges without any page count estimate, rush fees that exceed base pricing, separate charges for every component of the workflow, and long term contracts with volume minimums that punish normal caseload fluctuation.


It also pays to look at whether a platform is still being built on. Codes Health's MIT educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps getting more comprehensive as the demands on legal teams shift.


## **Bottom Line**


Lexitas gives you a clear number on the analysis side: $0.25 per uploaded page for Record Insights at its current introductory rate, with standard delivery in 2 to 5 business days. What you will not find publicly is a base retrieval rate, which means comparison starts with a quote request. And with a reported 30 to 45 day average retrieval turnaround plus separate analysis processing, the full picture takes some assembly.


For plaintiff firms running real caseloads, the meaningful measure is total cost of ownership rather than a single line item. A flat fee that already includes AI chronologies, human verified analysis, completeness verification, and embedded case management integration removes both the per page math and the internal hours that quietly stack up across a hundred cases. Speed on its own is not the win it appears to be either: same day delivery that returns partial records hands the chase back to your client, while complete records in a couple of weeks keep the case moving without the gaps.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How is medical record retrieval typically priced by services like Lexitas?**


Lexitas does not appear to publish a standard base rate for its main record retrieval service on its current public pages, so firms request quotes directly. For AI chronologies through Record Insights, Lexitas currently charges $0.25 per uploaded page as an introductory rate. Other providers use different structures: per facility charges (one vendor publishes $50 per medical record request on its Basic plan, plus a $150 case setup fee), per request flat fees (another publishes a $45 fixed fee for a typical request), and all inclusive flat fees that bundle retrieval with AI analysis, which is the Codes Health model. The variation in[pricing structures](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/software-solutions-plaintiff-law-firms) makes direct comparison hard without quotes tied to your own volume.


### **Does the speed of retrieval affect its overall cost?**


Speed affects case economics well beyond the retrieval invoice. A 30 to 45 day cycle pushes back demand letter preparation, expert engagement, and negotiation. For plaintiff practices where revenue depends on resolution velocity, faster retrieval accelerates cash flow even when per request pricing looks similar. Rush fees add explicit cost, while the implicit cost of delay in carrying costs, delayed fee realization, and client patience often exceeds the pricing difference between vendors.


### **Are AI analysis features included in base pricing or sold as add ons?**


It varies a lot. Lexitas sells Record Insights separately at $0.25 per uploaded page, with summaries delivered 2 to 5 business days after records are submitted for analysis. Codes Health includes AI automated chronologies, document summarization, insights extraction, and breach of care flagging in its flat fee, with no per page charge for analysis. For a 100 case practice averaging 1,000 pages per case, that distinction is worth roughly $25,000 a year in chronology fees alone.


### **What factors might increase or decrease the cost of medical record retrieval?**


Record volume drives per page charges where they apply. Multiple facilities extend timelines and can trigger additional requests. Authorization quality affects rejection rates, and a rejected authorization restarts the clock on that request. Rush requirements add expedite charges. Analysis needs add chronology cost wherever analysis is sold separately. Completeness problems requiring follow up create duplicate effort. AI authorization validation and Missing Record Review cut down several of these variable drivers by catching errors before submission and verifying completeness before delivery.


### **How can law firms make sure they are getting complete records?**


Completeness verification is one of the clearest differentiators among retrieval services. Traditional workflows often deliver whatever the provider returns without checking it against the original request, which leaves firms discovering missing facilities, date ranges, or record categories during case prep or, worse, at trial. Missing Record Review cross references returned materials against patient history and the original request to flag gaps before a retrieval is closed. Ask vendors directly whether completeness verification is included, how gaps get identified, and what the process is for supplemental records.
